description: Planet X and SPHEREx is a NASA Space Apps Challenge focused on exploring the universe using data from the SPHEREx space telescope. Participants create AI, data visualization, or software solutions to analyze planets, stars, and galaxies. The goal is to make space data easier to understand and discover new insights. The challenge encourages innovation using real NASA datasets.
summary:
Planet X, also known as **Planet Nine**, is a hypothetical planet believed to exist in the far outer region of our Solar System beyond Neptune. Although it has not yet been directly observed, astronomers have proposed its existence based on the unusual orbital patterns of several distant trans-Neptunian objects. If Planet X exists, it is estimated to be significantly larger than Earth and could provide valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the Solar System. Discovering it would be one of the most significant achievements in modern astronomy.

**SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer)** is a NASA space telescope designed to conduct an all-sky survey in infrared light. Its mission is to map hundreds of millions of galaxies, study the origins and evolution of the universe, investigate the formation of galaxies, and detect water ice and organic molecules within the Milky Way. The vast dataset generated by SPHEREx is publicly available for scientific research and educational purposes.

Although SPHEREx is not dedicated solely to finding Planet X, its infrared observations can help scientists identify faint and distant celestial objects that may be potential Planet X candidates.
